question.text: Kashi Ventures (Cat I) makes a follow-on investment in its Series B portfolio company at INR 200 crore pre-money. The fund's original Series A investment is on the books at cost. Per IPEV 2022 'Price of Previous Transaction' method, what is the correct valuation treatment for the Series A holding?

answer.text: Continue carrying Series A at original cost indefinitely
Mark the Series A holding up to reflect the Series B implied valuation
Mark the Series A down by 25% DLOM regardless of the follow-on
Wait for exit before any mark-up

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per PDF Section 11.8.3 point 1: 'When the AIF makes a follow-on investment in a company, the pricing thereof becomes the IMPLIED market value of the company which can be APPLIED TO THE ENTIRE INVESTMENT. However, for the FIRST investment, it needs to be carried at cost at that time and revised thereafter, based on pricing of follow-on investments.' So Series A gets marked up to Series B's implied valuation. **The Trap:** Holding indefinitely at cost ignores the new market signal; 25% DLOM is irrelevant to transaction pricing; waiting for exit is the pre-IPEV approach that IPEV explicitly replaced. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests identical treatment. XIX-B (Cat III) rarely faces this because Cat III is liquid. CFA L3 treats this under 'calibration' of PE marks. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** A genuine third-party priced round (e.g., external lead in Series B) is a stronger mark-up signal than an insider-only bridge round. Insider-only rounds should be marked up cautiously — some LP advisory boards require explicit approval for insider-priced mark-ups.
